question.text: An object moves with a uniform speed of 2 m/s for the first half of its total travel duration. Throughout the second half of the time, it covers ¼ of the distance traveled in that interval at a steady speed of 4 m/s, and the other ¾ of the distance at 6 m/s. Determine the average speed of the object over the entire journey.
conditions: motion for first half of total duration is at constant speed 2 m/s
motion for second half of total duration is split by distance: ¼ at 4 m/s and ¾ at 6 m/s

solution.approach: Write every distance in terms of the total time, add them up, and divide by the total time so the total time cancels out.

steps.text: Let the total time of the journey be T. In the first half of the time, T/2, the particle moves at 2 m/s.
In the second half of the time, T/2, the particle covers some distance d2, one quarter of it at 4 m/s and three quarters of it at 6 m/s; write the time for each part and add them to T/2.
Add the two distances to get the total distance covered.
Average speed is total distance divided by the total time T, and T cancels out.
steps.why_this_step: Since every distance was written proportional to T, the actual value of T never matters.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the plain average of the three speeds, (2 + 4 + 6)/3 = 4 m/s, instead of weighting each speed by the time or distance it actually covers.
Reading the 1/4 and 3/4 split as a split of the second half's time rather than its distance, which gives an average speed of 3.75 m/s instead of 11/3 m/s.
